title: Your first batch: calculating lye and making cold-process bars
course_title: Soap Making for Small Business: Cold-Process Bars and Simple Liquid Soap

say: Your first batch: calculating lye and making cold-process bars.
This is the video for Module 2 of Soap Making for Small Business.
Getting the lye amount right is what makes soap safe. Too much caustic soda leaves a harsh bar that can burn.

panel.heading: Getting the lye right keeps soap safe
items: Too much caustic soda: a harsh, burning bar
Too little: a greasy, soft bar that goes rancid
Calculate by hand, then check in SoapCalc
Never swap caustic soda and caustic potash

say: Too little leaves a greasy, soft bar that may go rancid.

say: And caustic soda and caustic potash have different SAP values. A recipe made for one can never be used with the other.

say: For example, Amaka plans 1,000 g of oils. Palm oil 500 g, palm kernel oil 300 g, shea butter 150 g and castor oil 50 g.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water

say: Step one. Multiply each oil by its SAP value. Palm oil is 500 times 0.142, which is 71.0 g of caustic soda. She does the same for each oil.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water

say: Step two. Add them all up. 71.0, plus 52.8, plus 19.2, plus 6.4, gives 149.4 g.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water

say: Step three. Apply the superfat. Superfat is a little oil left on purpose as a safety margin. For 5%, multiply by 0.95. That gives 141.9 g.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water

say: Step four. Work out the water. Divide the lye by 0.33, which gives 430.0 g of solution, then take away the lye. That leaves 288.1 g of water.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water

say: So Amaka weighs 142 g of caustic soda and 288 g of water. Never round the lye up by more than a gram.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water

say: Then she enters the same recipe into SoapCalc. If the answers agree within a gram or two, she is ready. A big difference means a mistake.

panel.heading: Amaka calculates her caustic soda
items: Each oil x its SAP value, e.g. palm 500 x 0.142
Add them up: 149.4 g at 0% superfat
Weigh 142 g caustic soda and 288 g water
panel.rule: Two calculations that agree give you confidence to mix.

say: Now the batch. Goggles, gloves and long sleeves on, children and pets out. Line your mould and gently melt the solid oils.

panel.heading: Making the batch
items: Safety gear on, mould lined, oils melted

Pour lye into oils; pulse 3 to 5 seconds, stir
Light trace: add fragrance, then pour
Rest 24 to 48 hours, cut, cure 4 to 6 weeks

say: Add caustic soda to the water, in a ventilated place. Many beginners combine when the lye and oils are both between 35 and 45 degrees Celsius. Write both temperatures down.

say: Pour the lye slowly into the oils down the blender shaft. Pulse the stick blender for 3 to 5 seconds, stir, and repeat.

say: Leave it covered for 24 to 48 hours, away from children. Then cut into bars and cure them on a rack for 4 to 6 weeks, turning them every few days.

say: Until the reaction finishes, the batter can burn skin. Keep gloves on, and never let anyone touch or taste fresh soap.

panel.rule: Fresh soap is still caustic. Gloves on until it is curing.

say: If the batter suddenly thickens and goes lumpy, called seizing, it is often the fragrance or mixing too hot. Press it into the mould quickly and note it in your record.

panel.heading: Problems on the day
items: Sudden lumps (seizing): work fast, note fragrance
Oil pools and will not trace: check your weighing
Cracks or a wet dark patch: soap overheated

say: If oil pools on top and will not trace, check that you weighed the caustic soda correctly. If you are not sure, do not sell this batch.

say: Cracks or a dark wet patch after a day mean it overheated. In hot weather, skip the towel and keep the mould in a cool room.

say: People call two different products liquid soap. True liquid soap is cooked from oils and potassium hydroxide into a paste, then diluted with hot water. All the caustic soda safety rules apply.

panel.heading: Two kinds of liquid soap
left: Cooked to a paste, then diluted

say: The keg wash is a liquid detergent made from SLES, often sold as texapon. You dilute it in water and thicken it with salt, a little at a time. Too much salt makes it thin again.
Both can be good products. Just label each one honestly.

panel.heading: Two kinds of liquid soap
left: Cooked to a paste, then diluted

say: Wear gloves and goggles for both routes.

panel.heading: Three safety rules for liquid products

cards.d: SLES paste irritates eyes and skin. Caustic potash needs full lye safety.
Use a cosmetic preservative at the supplier's stated rate. Never formalin.
Check a filled bottle daily for separation, cloudiness, smell or mould.

say: Some local recipes add formalin as a preservative. Formaldehyde is classified as a cancer-causing substance. Use a proper cosmetic preservative instead.

panel.heading: Three safety rules for liquid products

cards.d: SLES paste irritates eyes and skin. Caustic potash needs full lye safety.

Check a filled bottle daily for separation, cloudiness, smell or mould.

say: And test every new recipe for a week before you sell it, checking each day for separation, cloudiness, a smell change or mould.

say: To remember. Lye is oil weight times SAP value. Multiply by 0.95 for a 5% superfat. Always check in SoapCalc. Combine warm, cure fully, and never use formalin.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Lye = oil weight x SAP value, for every oil
Multiply by 0.95 for a 5% superfat
Check your hand calculation in SoapCalc
Combine at about 35 to 45 °C, cure 4 to 6 weeks
Liquid products need a proper preservative
